ai.title: Remove async knowledge file generation from backend prompt
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts deletes `genKnowledgeFilesPromise` and associated `generateKnowledgeFiles` calls. `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` updates `getResponseFormatPrompt` to accept `fileContext` and injects knowledge file instructions directly into the system prompt. Scope covers backend prompt logic. `main-prompt.ts` now emits 'No changes to existing files.' if `fileProcessingPromises` yield no changes.

eli5.text: The assistant now decides what file context to include by reading the system prompt directly, instead of generating knowledge files in a separate background step. When it looked at your project, it would quietly build a set of reference files while also replying to you; now it gathers that context up front and weaves it into the instructions it reads before it answers. You would notice this only in the internal timing of how your project is processed, not in what shows up on your screen. This is already live in the internal build.

ai.title: System prompt adds explicit permission check for permanent scripts
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated to require explicit user permission before running scripts with permanent effects or production impacts. The guidelines list was renumbered to accommodate the new constraint, and the 'Running scripts' use case now includes a warning about permanent effects. This change affects the agent's internal decision-making logic for terminal command execution.

eli5.text: The assistant now has to ask you before it runs any script that could permanently change your project or affect live systems, like running a setup or deployment script. This applies to scripts written directly into your project as well as ones pulled from your project's command list. If you ask the assistant to do something that requires it to run such a script, you will now get a prompt requesting your explicit go-ahead before anything happens.

ai.title: tiktoken 1.0.17, package-lock.json removed
ai.summary: tiktoken bumped 1.0.15 to 1.0.17 in backend/package.json. package-lock.json deleted in favor of bun.lockb. Scope backend deps, lockfile. Migration: bun install required, no npm lock.

eli5.text: The tool the assistant uses to count words in your messages was quietly updated, and the project's package list was rebuilt using a different tool. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance that doesn't change anything you see or feel when chatting. If you're a developer on the backend team, you'll need to reinstall dependencies with the new package manager before the changes take effect.

ai.title: Remove unused backend build and test scripts from package.json
ai.summary: Removed prebuild, postbuild, clean, test, test:manifold, and test:watch scripts from backend/package.json. Only the build script remains. This cleans up unused or redundant commands in the backend package configuration.

eli5.text: The team removed several old, unused setup commands that told the system how to build and test its own code, leaving only the main build command. These leftover commands were harmless clutter that nobody was running anymore, so their removal makes the setup file shorter and easier to understand. You wouldn't notice any difference in how the software works today, but the internal configuration is now cleaner and simpler.

ai.title: CLI exit requires double Ctrl-C
ai.summary: Pressing Ctrl-C now requires two presses within 3 seconds to exit. First press shows 'Press Ctrl-C again to exit' and re-prompts. Second press triggers handleExit().

eli5.text: If you press Ctrl-C once while using Codebuff at the command line, instead of immediately quitting, it will now print 'Press Ctrl-C again to exit' and wait. You must press Ctrl-C a second time within 3 seconds for Codebuff to actually close; otherwise, it treats the first press as if you changed your mind and keeps running. The menu text also now tells you upfront that pressing Ctrl-C twice exits Codebuff. This change is live today for anyone running Codebuff from the terminal.

ai.title: Detect homebrew/bin as npm installer
ai.summary: Update detectInstaller in npm-app/src/update-codebuff.ts to include /opt/homebrew/bin/codebuff in global npm path detection. Adds homebrew/bin string check to isGlobalNpmPath condition. Ensures Homebrew-installed binaries are correctly identified as npm installs.

eli5.text: When the tool starts up, it now recognizes installations made through Homebrew's bin directory as valid npm installs, so you won’t see false warnings if you used Homebrew to install it. The system that figures out how you installed the software learned one new path to check, alongside the existing ones for direct npm installs and Node Version Manager setups. This fix is live today for anyone who installs via Homebrew on systems where Homebrew places binaries under /opt/homebrew/bin.

ai.title: Add system info to project context
ai.summary: System info (platform, shell, node version, arch, homedir, cpus) injected into ProjectFileContext via new systemInfo schema in common/src/util/file.ts and collected in npm-app/src/project-files.ts. Replaces getMiscFilesPrompt with getSystemInfoPrompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts, restructuring prompt to lead with OS/Shell details before shell config files and recently read paths. Covers backend, common, and npm-app packages; requires systemInfo object for all project context consumers.

eli5.text: The assistant can now see basic details about your computer before you even ask a question. When you open a project, it automatically learns which operating system and command-line program you are using (like Windows Command Prompt or a Mac terminal), how many processor chips your machine has, and where your main folder lives. This information now appears at the top of what the assistant reads about your project, right alongside the file list and recent files, so it can give more helpful answers without you having to explain your setup.

ai.title: Version 1.0.119
ai.summary: Bumped npm-app package version to 1.0.119. Change limited to npm-app/package.json. No functional code modifications.

eli5.text: Today, updating to the latest version of the assistant lowers the price of the top-tier subscription plans, Pro is now $49 and Pro Plus is $249, alongside a small set of behind-the-scenes tweaks that make file handling and knowledge updates run more smoothly. The most noticeable change for you is the halved subscription price, which applies to anyone buying or renewing a Pro or Pro Plus plan starting now. The rest of the update is invisible housekeeping: the assistant skips certain caching steps during single-file searches, applies stricter rules before refreshing its knowledge files, switches one model used for finding relevant files, and cleans up a few internal commands so exits need two quick presses of Ctrl-C instead of one. If you looked, you would only see the new lower prices;

ai.title: Add latencyms tracking to message cost schema
ai.summary: Added `latency_ms` column to the `message` table via migration `0010_overjoyed_red_skull.sql`. Updated `saveMessage` in `message-cost-tracker.ts` to accept and store `latencyMs`. Instrumented `promptClaudeStreamWithoutRetry` in `claude.ts` and `promptOpenAI`/`promptOpenAIWithContinuation` in `openai-api.ts` to capture request start time and calculate duration.

eli5.text: Each message sent to a request now records how long it took to get an answer back. When you look at a past message in the system, the time it spent waiting for a response is shown alongside other details like cost. This only affects messages processed after the latest update.
